title: No Keel Artifact edit may violate the Sky Core Atlas, and enforcing that limit is the Facilitator's review mandate
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.6 states the substantive limit on Agent self-governance: "the Keel Artifact cannot be edited in any way that violates the Sky Core Atlas or its specifications of the Sky Primitives, or in any way that is otherwise misaligned. The Operational Facilitator must enforce this rule through their review of Artifact Edit Proposals."

This is the clause that gives the alignment review its content. Two of the three prohibitions are checkable against text — the Atlas and the Primitive specifications are written documents — while the third, "otherwise misaligned," is open-textured and imports the Atlas's whole doctrine of Universal Alignment as a residual catch-all.

The asymmetry is deliberate and matches the Atlas's stance elsewhere on letter-versus-spirit reading: a rule that only forbade textual violations could be walked around by an edit that satisfies every provision while defeating their purpose. The residual clause closes that gap at the cost of giving the reviewer discretion no text fully constrains.

The structural consequence is that an Agent Artifact is a subordinate document by construction. Keel's tokenholders own the Agent's strategy but not its constitutional frame, and the Primitives they operate through are specified upstream where Keel Governance cannot reach them.
description: Artifact Edit Restrictions bar any edit that breaks the Atlas, its Sky Primitive specifications, or is 'otherwise misaligned' — defining what the pre-vote alignment review is actually checking.
